outputs.reference_answer:
1. Lineage of cost: seeds/pharma/drugs.csv:13 holds `12,Losartan,10.60,30,ARB,false`; `dbt seed` loads it into the land_raw source (models/landing_raw/pharma/sources.yml:4-9 declares land_raw.drugs). models/landing/pharma/land_drugs.sql:6 `cast(cost as decimal(18,2)) as cost`, reading source('land_raw','drugs') at line 10. snapshots/ods_hist/pharma/drugs_snapshot.sql:6 selects cost from ref('land_drugs') (line 10); dbt_project.yml:48-50 makes it a check snapshot on all columns keyed by id, so a cost change closes the old row and opens a new current row. models/staging/pharma/stg_dispensing.sql:87-94 drug_current reads ref('drugs_snapshot') (line 92), casts cost (line 91) and keeps only rows where dbt_valid_to is 9999-12-31 (line 93); line 103 exposes it as drug_cost via the left join on d.id = p.drug_id (lines 109-110); line 119 selects drug_cost. models/reporting/pharma/rep_dispensing.sql:3-4 is `select * from ref('stg_dispensing')`.
2. Only drug_cost changes (10.60 to 15.00) and only on rows whose drug_id is 12. drug_name is unchanged (the name is unchanged). prescription_cost comes from the prescription's own total_cost (stg_dispensing.sql:9, 26, 106), not from drug cost, so it does not change; subsidy_amount, drug_frequency, patient_id, patient_name, gender, nhi and prescription_id are unchanged.
3. The rows for prescriptions with drug_id 12 in seeds/pharma/prescription.csv: prescription 22 (patient 11), prescription 23 (patient 12, dated 2026-07-15, i.e. historical) and prescription 52 (patient 26). Past-dated prescriptions are affected too, because the drug join has no date condition — as long as the prescription passes the snapshot validity filter at stg_dispensing.sql:13-14. Patients with no prescriptions come from current_patients_without_prescriptions (lines 36-55) with a null drug_id (line 42), so the left join finds no drug and their drug_cost stays null: unaffected.
4. The report shows the drug's current cost, not the cost valid at prescription time: stg_dispensing.sql:93 keeps only the current snapshot row (dbt_valid_to = 9999-12-31) and lines 109-110 join on id alone, unlike prescriptions (lines 13-14) and patients (lines 32-33), which are joined point-in-time.
5. Edit seeds/pharma/drugs.csv:13, then in DAG order: `dbt seed --select drugs`, `dbt run --select land_drugs`, `dbt snapshot --select drugs_snapshot`, then `dbt run --select stg_dispensing rep_dispensing`. `dbt build --select <model>` can be used for each explicitly named stage (`dbt build --select drugs_snapshot` runs the snapshot). A single `dbt build --select drugs+` is not equivalent here: land_drugs reads source('land_raw', 'drugs'), so the seed has no declared edge to that landing model. Keep the explicit stages. Skipping the seed load, or snapshotting before land_drugs is rebuilt, is wrong.

Lineage of cost: seeds/pharma/drugs.csv:13 holds `12,Losartan,10.60,30,ARB,false`; `dbt seed` loads it into the land_raw source (models/landing_raw/pharma/sources.yml:4-9 declares land_raw.drugs). models/landing/pharma/land_drugs.sql:6 `cast(cost as decimal(18,2)) as cost`, reading source('land_raw','drugs') at line 10. snapshots/ods_hist/pharma/drugs_snapshot.sql:6 selects cost from ref('land_drugs') (line 10); dbt_project.yml:48-50 makes it a check snapshot on all columns keyed by id, so a cost change closes the old row and opens a new current row. models/staging/pharma/stg_dispensing.sql:87-94 drug_current reads ref('drugs_snapshot') (line 92), casts cost (line 91) and keeps only rows where dbt_valid_to is 9999-12-31 (line 93); line 103 exposes it as drug_cost via the left join on d.id = p.drug_id (lines 109-110); line 119 selects drug_cost. models/reporting/pharma/rep_dispensing.sql:3-4 is `select * from ref('stg_dispensing')`.
2. Only drug_cost changes (10.60 to 15.00) and only on rows whose drug_id is 12. drug_name is unchanged (the name is unchanged). prescription_cost comes from the prescription's own total_cost (stg_dispensing.sql:9, 26, 106), not from drug cost, so it does not change; subsidy_amount, drug_frequency, patient_id, patient_name, gender, nhi and prescription_id are unchanged.
3. The rows for prescriptions with drug_id 12 in seeds/pharma/prescription.csv: prescription 22 (patient 11), prescription 23 (patient 12, dated 2026-07-15, i.e. historical) and prescription 52 (patient 26). Past-dated prescriptions are affected too, because the drug join has no date condition — as long as the prescription passes the snapshot validity filter at stg_dispensing.sql:13-14. Patients with no prescriptions come from current_patients_without_prescriptions (lines 36-55) with a null drug_id (line 42), so the left join finds no drug and their drug_cost stays null: unaffected.
4. The report shows the drug's current cost, not the cost valid at prescription time: stg_dispensing.sql:93 keeps only the current snapshot row (dbt_valid_to = 9999-12-31) and lines 109-110 join on id alone, unlike prescriptions (lines 13-14) and patients (lines 32-33), which are joined point-in-time.
5. Edit seeds/pharma/drugs.csv:13, then in DAG order: `dbt seed --select drugs`, `dbt run --select land_drugs`, `dbt snapshot --select drugs_snapshot`, then `dbt run --select stg_dispensing rep_dispensing`. `dbt build --select <model>` can be used for each explicitly named stage (`dbt build --select drugs_snapshot` runs the snapshot). A single `dbt build --select drugs+` is not equivalent here: land_drugs reads source('land_raw', 'drugs'), so the seed has no declared edge to that landing model. Keep the explicit stages. Skipping the seed load, or snapshotting before land_drugs is rebuilt, is wrong.
